anchor_names.description: This attack utilizes a REST(REpresentational State Transfer)-style applications' trust in the system resources and environment to obtain sensitive data once SSL is terminated.

question: What severity is typically assigned to the CAPEC attack pattern known as Fuzzing (CAPEC-28)?

anchor_names.name: Fuzzing
anchor_names.description: In this attack pattern, the adversary leverages fuzzing to try to identify weaknesses in the system. Fuzzing is a software security and functionality testing method that feeds randomly constructed input to the system and looks for an indication that a failure in response to that input has occurred.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which CAPEC attack patterns is Flash Injection (CAPEC-182) a more specific case of?

anchor_names.name: Flash Injection
anchor_names.description: An attacker tricks a victim to execute malicious flash content that executes commands or makes flash calls specified by the attacker. One example of this attack is cross-site flashing, an attacker controlled parameter to a reference call loads from content specified by the attacker.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which CAPEC attack patterns is the attack pattern Collect Data from Clipboard CAPEC-637 a specific case of?

anchor_names.name: Collect Data from Clipboard
anchor_names.description: The adversary exploits an application that allows for the copying of sensitive data or information by collecting information copied to the clipboard. Data copied to the clipboard can be accessed by other applications, such as malware built to exfiltrate or log clipboard contents on a periodic basis.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which CWE weaknesses does the CAPEC attack pattern known as Input Data Manipulation (CAPEC-153) exploit?

anchor_names.name: Input Data Manipulation
anchor_names.description: An attacker exploits a weakness in input validation by controlling the format, structure, and composition of data to an input-processing interface. By supplying input of a non-standard or unexpected form an attacker can adversely impact the security of the target.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which CWE weaknesses does System Footprinting (CAPEC-580) exploit?

anchor_names.name: System Footprinting
anchor_names.description: An adversary engages in active probing and exploration activities to determine security information about a remote target system. Often times adversaries will rely on remote applications that can be probed for system configurations.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern
